# Meṇḍakapañhajātaka (Ja 471)

**ID:** Ja 471
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Meṇḍakapañhajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul11.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Epigraphic and artistic evidence from the Pagan period in Burma demonstrates that the story was regularly identified and depicted in temple illustrations [WinThanTun 2002]. In Pagan-era temple plaques and inscriptions, the Jātaka appears under several variant titles and spellings, including *Mendakapañha* (found at Winido and Shwezigon), *Mendapañha* (at Ajagona, Chaukhpayahla, and Gubyaukgyi [Myinkaba]), *Mindapañha* (at Thingaraza and Thambula), *Mendoka* (at Gubyaukgyi [Wetkyi-in]), and *Siriminda* (at the Ananda Temple) [WinThanTun 2002].

**Sources**

- [WinThanTun 2002] Win Than Tun, Buddhism Pagan period (2002) — Pagan-era temple inscriptions, depictions, and title variants (Mendapañha, Mindapañha, Mendoka, Siriminda)
